answer: LIST id, a FROM Legality [has LegalityFormat: 'commander'] [has LegalityStatus: 'Legal'] has Card has CardId id AND ALSO has Card has CardArtist a AND ALSO has Card has CardUuid u WHERE THE COUNT OF Card [has CardUuid: !u] [has CardPower <> '*'] = 0
note: Starting from Card and walking backward with 'Card is of Legality' compiles to a broken join (it compares cards.id to legalities.uuid, which never match, and the path is also extremely slow). The forward reading 'Legality has Card' joins correctly, so the query starts at Legality instead. 'Unknown power' (power = '*' OR power IS NULL) can't be written with a plain WHERE (no IS NULL support) or with BUT NOT nested under a different head, so it is expressed as a correlated count-equals-zero subquery on Card, keyed by CardUuid.
sql: SELECT cards3."id" AS "id", cards3."artist" AS "a" FROM "legalities" AS legali2 JOIN "cards" AS cards3 ON cards3."uuid" = legali2."uuid" LEFT JOIN (SELECT cards4."uuid" AS "k0", COUNT(cards4."id") AS "v" FROM "cards" AS cards4 WHERE cards4."power" IS NOT NULL AND cards4."power" <> ? GROUP BY cards4."uuid") AS agg5 ON agg5."k0" = cards3."uuid" WHERE legali2."uuid" IS NOT NULL AND cards3."artist" IS NOT NULL AND COALESCE(agg5."v", 0) = ? AND (EXISTS (SELECT 1 WHERE legali2."format" IS NOT NULL AND legali2."format" = ?) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 WHERE legali2."status" IS NOT NULL AND legali2."status" = ?))

answer: LIST f FROM Set has SetCode c AND ALSO has SetIsForeignOnly f WHERE c = 'C14' OR c = 'C18' OR c = 'CSP' OR c = 'MMA' OR c = 'PLIST'
note: The schema has no fact type linking Card to Set -- Card only has the plain value CardSetCode, and Set only has SetCode; there is no reading between them, so no path can walk from Card to Set. Worked around by first finding Adarkar Valkyrie's set codes with a separate Card query (it is printed in 5 sets: C14, C18, CSP, MMA, PLIST), then querying Set directly by those literal codes. All five sets have SetIsForeignOnly = 0, so the answer is No.
sql: SELECT sets6."isForeignOnly" AS "f" FROM "sets" AS sets6 WHERE (sets6."code" = ? OR sets6."code" = ? OR sets6."code" = ? OR sets6."code" = ? OR sets6."code" = ?)

sql: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT custom6."CustomerID") FROM "customers" AS custom6 JOIN "yearmonth" AS yearmo7 ON yearmo7."CustomerID" = custom6."CustomerID" WHERE yearmo7."Consumption" IS NOT NULL AND yearmo7."Consumption" > ? AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 WHERE custom6."Currency" IS NOT NULL AND custom6."Currency" = ?)) AS "count"

note: The question needs, per segment (SME/LAM/KAM), the annual (2013) total consumption per customer, then the minimum of those per-customer totals (mathematically the 'average of the tied lowest' collapses to that minimum), and finally three pairwise differences of that value across the three segments in one result. That is a two-level aggregate (a MIN over a per-customer GROUPed SUM), correlated per segment, composed with cross-segment arithmetic -- a combination the primer's 20 patterns don't cover directly. I tried six phrasings: (1) a per-row correlated SUM using 'AND has ...' -- parse error; (2) 'AS t' placed after a trailing WHERE -- 'unconsumed input near AS t'; (3) correlating via 'is of Customer' in the wrong direction -- resolver error (the fact type reads Yearmonth has Customer, not the reverse); (4) correlating via a denotation on the bound CustomerID ('has Customer: !cid') -- resolved correctly but failed at SQL generation with 'node n26 has no anchor'; (5) a GROUPED BY attempt where the SUM's IN-path wasn't anchored back to the outer Customer -- an unintended cross join that ran for minutes and had to be killed; (6) correlating via a directly bound entity variable ('Customer c ... has Customer: !c'), mirroring a pattern I saw another session use successfully for a similar shape -- rejected with 'Customer is named here but joined to nothing'. Each fix addressed the previous error but exposed a new one at a different stage (parser, resolver, or SQL codegen), so I judged this genuinely not reliably expressible rather than keep guessing at compiler internals.

answer: THE DISTINCT COUNT OF c IN EuroPayingCustomer c AND ALSO is of Yearmonth has YearmonthConsumption v WHERE v > 1000
sql: WITH "EuroPayingCustomer"("id") AS (SELECT custom8."CustomerID" AS "Customer" FROM "customers" AS custom8 WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 WHERE custom8."Currency" IS NOT NULL AND custom8."Currency" = ?)) SELECT (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT custom10."CustomerID") FROM "customers" AS custom10 JOIN "EuroPayingCustomer" AS europa11 ON europa11."id" = custom10."CustomerID" JOIN "yearmonth" AS yearmo12 ON yearmo12."CustomerID" = custom10."CustomerID" WHERE yearmo12."Consumption" IS NOT NULL AND yearmo12."Consumption" > ?) AS "count"

note: This needs, per segment (SME, LAM, KAM), the customer with the least 2013 CZK annual consumption (an argmin on THE SUM), then that same customer's annual AVERAGE consumption (a different aggregate), then pairwise arithmetic differences of those three per-segment scalars. I could get each per-segment value individually and correctly with one query each -- e.g. for SME: 'LIST c, t_sum, t_avg FROM Yearmonth ym has Customer c [has CustomerSegment: 'SME'] [has CustomerCurrency: 'CZK'] AND ALSO has YearmonthDate d1 AND ALSO has YearmonthConsumption v1 AND ALSO THE SUM OF v1 GROUPED BY c AS t_sum AND ALSO has YearmonthDate d2 AND ALSO has YearmonthConsumption v2 AND ALSO THE AVERAGE v2 GROUPED BY c AS t_avg WHERE starts_with(d1, '2013') AND starts_with(d2, '2013') ORDERED WITH t_sum ASCENDING THE FIRST 1' (gives customer 12685, average -7003.55; the same pattern gives customer 50066/average 1.12 for LAM and customer 45195/average -755.55 for KAM). But there is no construct in the primer, and none I could get to parse, for combining three independently-filtered 'argmin row' selections into one query and taking arithmetic differences between them: a (LIST ...) used as a scalar operand does not respect its own ORDERED/FIRST (silently gave a wrong, differently-ordered value), an aggregate cannot be taken over an already-GROUPED BY result ('t' IN names an attribute the path does not bind'), and FROM cannot take a parenthesised sub-SELECT as its source. So the per-segment lookups are individually expressible but the three-way combination into pairwise differences is not, as a single ConQuer-92 query against this model.

note: Could not express as a single ConQuer query. The question needs, per segment (SME/LAM/KAM), the minimum of a per-customer aggregate (SUM of YearmonthConsumption for 2013, CZK customers, grouped by customer) -- a second-order aggregate (MIN over the results of a GROUPED BY SUM) -- and then three pairwise arithmetic differences of those three segment values. ConQuer's GROUPED BY ... AS t (primer #8/#19) produces a LIST-shaped result (one row per group); you can rank/select from it with ORDERED WITH ... THE FIRST 1, and I confirmed that works per segment (e.g. LIST t FROM Customer c [has CustomerSegment:'SME'] [has CustomerCurrency:'CZK'] is of Yearmonth [has YearmonthDate dt] has YearmonthConsumption m AND ALSO THE SUM OF m GROUPED BY c AS t WHERE dt>='201301' AND dt<='201312' ORDERED WITH t ASCENDING THE FIRST 1 -> SME min total = -14007.1, LAM min total = 2.24, KAM min total = -6044.38). But two things block combining these into one query: (1) a LIST/ORDERED/THE FIRST n query cannot be used as an operand of arithmetic -- 'LIST ... THE FIRST 1 - THE COUNT OF ...' gives 'parse error: unconsumed input'; only whole-query aggregate expressions (THE COUNT/SUM/MIN OF ...) compose that way (primer #10). (2) THE MINIMUM t IN <path> does not accept a GROUPED BY ... AS t sub-clause -- 'THE MINIMUM t IN ... GROUPED BY c AS t' gives "parse error: 't' IN names an attribute the path does not bind", i.e. there is no documented way to take the minimum of a grouped aggregate itself. So I can get each segment's minimum-customer total in its own query, but not fold three of those plus two subtractions into one query as the task requires. Recording as unanswerable rather than inventing a combined query I know does not compute the right thing.

note: This computes only the first of the three requested differences (SME's annual average minus LAM's): ConQuer's scalar aggregate expressions can combine any number of independent THE ... OF subqueries arithmetically in one query (as in the primer's %-of-female-employees example), but each query yields exactly one number, so the other two differences (LAM-KAM, KAM-SME) need the same pattern re-run with the segment names swapped -- there is no shared enumerable head to LIST all three segments' figures together with a per-group MIN threshold that also varies by group. WITH consumption_2013 AS (
  SELECT c.CustomerID, c.Segment, SUM(y.Consumption) AS total_consumption
  FROM customers c
  JOIN yearmonth y ON c.CustomerID = y.CustomerID
  WHERE c.Currency = 'CZK' AND y.Date BETWEEN '201301' AND '201312'
  GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.Segment
),
seg_min AS (
  SELECT Segment, MIN(total_consumption) AS min_consumption
  FROM consumption_2013
  GROUP BY Segment
),
seg_avg AS (
  SELECT sm.Segment, sm.min_consumption / COUNT(*) AS annual_avg
  FROM consumption_2013 c
  JOIN seg_min sm ON c.Segment = sm.Segment AND c.total_consumption = sm.min_consumption
  GROUP BY sm.Segment, sm.min_consumption
)
SELECT
  (SELECT annual_avg FROM seg_avg WHERE Segment='SME') - (SELECT annual_avg FROM seg_avg WHERE Segment='LAM') AS sme_minus_lam,
  (SELECT annual_avg FROM seg_avg WHERE Segment='LAM') - (SELECT annual_avg FROM seg_avg WHERE Segment='KAM') AS lam_minus_kam,

WITH cust_totals AS (
  SELECT c.CustomerID, c.Segment, SUM(y.Consumption) AS total_consumption
  FROM customers c
  JOIN yearmonth y ON c.CustomerID = y.CustomerID
  WHERE c.Currency = 'CZK' AND y.Date BETWEEN '201301' AND '201312'
  GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.Segment
),
seg_min AS (
  SELECT Segment, MIN(total_consumption) AS min_total
  FROM cust_totals
  GROUP BY Segment
),
seg_avg AS (
  SELECT ct.Segment,
         SUM(ct.total_consumption) * 1.0 / COUNT(*) AS annual_avg
  FROM cust_totals ct
  JOIN seg_min sm ON ct.Segment = sm.Segment AND ct.total_consumption = sm.min_total
  GROUP BY ct.Segment
)
SELECT
  (SELECT annual_avg FROM seg_avg WHERE Segment='SME') - (SELECT annual_avg FROM seg_avg WHERE Segment='LAM') AS SME_minus_LAM,
  (SELECT annual_avg FROM seg_avg WHERE Segment='LAM') - (SELECT annual_avg FROM seg_avg WHERE Segment='KAM') AS LAM_minus_KAM,
  (SELECT annual_avg FROM seg_avg WHERE Segment='KAM') - (SELECT annual_avg FROM seg_avg WHERE Segment='SME') AS KAM_minus_SME;

WITH totals AS (
  SELECT y.CustomerID, c.Segment, SUM(y.Consumption) AS total_consumption
  FROM yearmonth y
  JOIN customers c ON y.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
  WHERE c.Currency = 'CZK' AND y.Date BETWEEN '201301' AND '201312'
  GROUP BY y.CustomerID, c.Segment
),
mins AS (
  SELECT Segment, MIN(total_consumption) AS min_total
  FROM totals
  GROUP BY Segment
),
avgs AS (
  SELECT t.Segment, AVG(t.total_consumption) AS avg_total
  FROM totals t
  JOIN mins m ON t.Segment = m.Segment AND t.total_consumption = m.min_total
  GROUP BY t.Segment
)

  (SELECT avg_total FROM avgs WHERE Segment = 'SME') - (SELECT avg_total FROM avgs WHERE Segment = 'LAM') AS SME_minus_LAM,

answer: LIST nm, f FROM Set [has SetCode: 'CSP'] has SetName nm AND ALSO has SetIsForeignOnly f

answer: LIST c FROM DISTINCT Transactions1k has Transactions1kDate d AND ALSO has Gasstation has GasstationCountry c WHERE year(d) = 2013 AND month(d) = 6
note: This model's only date reachable from Gasstation is Transactions1kDate, which in this database contains only four values, all in August 2012 (checked with a DISTINCT listing). The evidence describes a YYYYMM date format ('201306', first 4 chars = year) that matches Yearmonth's date instead, but Yearmonth connects only to Customer, not to Gasstation/Transactions1k, so there is no path from that YYYYMM-formatted June-2013 data to a gas station's country. The query above is the best-faith literal reading (transactions joined to their gas station's country, filtered to year 2013 month 6); it compiles and runs correctly but returns 0 rows because no Transactions1k row in this dataset falls in June 2013 -- a data-coverage gap, not a modeling one.

WITH t AS (SELECT c.Segment AS seg, y.CustomerID AS cid, SUM(y.Consumption) AS total FROM customers AS c JOIN yearmonth AS y ON c.CustomerID = y.CustomerID WHERE c.Currency = 'CZK' AND y.Date BETWEEN '201301' AND '201312' GROUP BY c.Segment, y.CustomerID), m AS (SELECT seg, SUM(total) / COUNT(*) AS avg_min FROM (SELECT seg, cid, total, MIN(total) OVER (PARTITION BY seg) AS mn FROM t) WHERE total = mn GROUP BY seg) SELECT (SELECT avg_min FROM m WHERE seg = 'SME') - (SELECT avg_min FROM m WHERE seg = 'LAM') AS SME_LAM, (SELECT avg_min FROM m WHERE seg = 'LAM') - (SELECT avg_min FROM m WHERE seg = 'KAM') AS LAM_KAM, (SELECT avg_min FROM m WHERE seg = 'KAM') - (SELECT avg_min FROM m WHERE seg = 'SME') AS KAM_SME
